title: The portable masked scan is 3 to 8% slower since 55daf88
body:
`PrefixEncoder::compact` builds a suffix's masked key one field at a time. `build` uses it for seed-mask builds on aarch64 and on x86 CPUs without BMI2. Other x86 CPUs run `compact_pext`. Commit `55daf88` replaced the `PEXT` const generic on `count_masked` and `gather_masked` with a closure argument, `|w| encoder.compact(w)`. Commit `bbe52ae` made the pext functions safe and raised `rust-version` to 1.87. The pext path kept its speed. The portable path got slower.

The run used the benchmark suite on the `bench` branch at `398bcb9`: 100 MiB fixtures, 4 threads, median of 5, an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D. The portable builds force `has_bmi2` to `false`. Every build wrote the same output. A second run of the `6e81e38` portable build, in an earlier run of the suite, gave 5.64, 8.77 and 5.17 s on the three mask rows, within 1% of the run below.

| row | `6e81e38` | `bbe52ae` | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mask-dna` | 5.60 s | 5.92 s | +5.7% |
| `mask-dna-heavy` | 8.73 s | 9.03 s | +3.4% |
| `mask-protein` | 5.12 s | 5.52 s | +7.8% |
| `normal` | 1.42 s | 1.33 s | -6.3% |

Jack expects this may close as not worth fixing.

## Open

- Which of the two commits causes it. Only `6e81e38` against `bbe52ae` was measured.
- Whether the closure changes the generated code. Nobody has compared instructions or cycles.
close_reason: Jack does not consider the portable masked path worth chasing. Commits 023778c and 9f9c913 also replaced the code measured here. The current portable path, count_chunk with MaskedKeys::masked_key, has not been timed, and a later performance pass can measure it.
